feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (the only raced design) had 0 completions in 60 trials, max_error 0.060 to 0.064 m against the 0.06 m limit, rms_error 0.024 to 0.030 m, and 1.0 to 1.55 line-loss events per run. So the limit is peak excursion on bends, not average tracking, and the next design should target peaks. This package keeps your seven-sensor 0.12 m span, 16 mm footprint and 0.6 kg mass unchanged. For the integration questions: the span and footprint answers, and whether the 0.6 kg mass adds oscillation, can only be answered by the next race's steering_oscillation and max_error by track. The controller uses weights of ±1.5 at the outer sensors and kd 0.5 to damp the faster turn response from lower mass, so any oscillation at speed would show as steering_oscillation rising on the oval. Lower base_speed (1.0) was chosen to protect against the extra mass-driven oscillation and the untested geometry, so completion_time will show whether speed is now the constraint. Next race, if max_error is still above 0.06 m on the s-bend with line_loss_events of 1 or more, the sensing span is probably not the limit: then try a smaller footprint (12 mm) to sharpen the edge reading. If steering_oscillation is high on the oval and max_error is under 0.06 m, restore mass to 0.8 kg for more yaw damping. If completion_time is limiting and max_error is under 0.06 m, try a narrower wheel_track of 0.10 m to raise turn rate. Only one of these should change at a time so the next race can attribute the effect.
requested_changes: If max_error stays above 0.06 m on the s-bend and line_loss_events is 1 or more: change sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m to sharpen the edge reading. Evidence: iteration 0 showed the line lost on bends with a 12 mm footprint and 6 cm span, so the footprint change must be tested alone against this span.

If steering_oscillation is high on the oval while max_error is under 0.06 m: restore mass from 0.6 kg to 0.8 kg for more yaw damping. Evidence: iteration 0 steering_oscillation of 0.14 to 0.16 m with the 0.8 kg baseline, so the lower mass may raise it further.

If completion_time exceeds about 2.5 s with max_error under 0.06 m: reduce wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m to raise turn rate. Evidence: iteration 0 rms_error was small (0.024 to 0.030 m) while no run finished, so tracking is adequate and speed or turn rate is the next limit.
